title: Geopolitical risks, global market factors and dependence among regional sustainable investments and commodities
publisher: Quarterly Review of Economics and Finance 91, 94–111
summary: The paper studies how sustainable investment indices for North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific connect with energy, precious metal and industrial metal commodities. It finds asymmetric connectedness, significantly stronger during extreme downside and upside market conditions.
keyFindings: Total connectedness is significantly stronger during extreme market downturns and rallies.
Only the Asia-Pacific sustainable investment index receives more shocks than it transmits in normal conditions.
Geopolitical risks, business conditions, gold and fixed income markets and economic policy uncertainty predict return connectedness.
methods: Quantile VAR connectedness approach, with regression analysis of macro and geopolitical predictors.
